correctness.rationale: The normalization H=(sigma(n)-2n)/2 follows exactly by sign flipping. Since the anchor a is an odd square, sigma(a) is odd, giving an integer h and a strict interval hm+b<H<(h+1)m for b=C(sigma(m)-m)<m. All subset sums lie outside the interval. Exact inclusion-exclusion and prime-divisor averaging give the explicit cofactor density rhoY(1-(C+1)/Y); the telescoping 1/Y bound is unconditional. Square cofactors contribute O(sqrt X) and do not affect positive density. Fixed scaling by a gives the stated n-density. The packaged checks independently validate the explicit anchor and strict inequalities; they are not substituted for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Ross conjectured all odd nonsquare abundant integers satisfy signed perfection. Campbell refuted this with infinitely many prime-cofactor odd examples, but proved positive density only for an even family. The new positive-density theorem for odd nonsquare numbers is strictly stronger than either statement; full relevant preprint sections, Ross Conjecture 17, exact-phrase searches, claim-specific semantic searches and own current/prior claim ledgers were compared.

value.rationale: Ross Conjecture 17 singled out the odd nonsquare abundant class; Campbell established infinitely many counterexamples there but proved positive density only on an even subfamily. Establishing positive density among the odd nonsquares answers a natural and qualitatively stronger quantitative question, supplies a general theorem for all odd abundant square anchors and an explicit numerical lower bound. This is not a routine finite slice or a numerical increment.
